scenarioStory.history: Patient was watching television when he developed sudden, severe 'tearing' chest pain that immediately radiated straight through to his upper back between the shoulder blades. Pain has remained constant at 10/10 since onset roughly 20 minutes ago, not positional, not reproducible with palpation. Denies exertion or trauma preceding the pain.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 65-year-old male with sudden-onset severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back, pale and diaphoretic, with a markedly elevated and asymmetric blood pressure between arms. → Pulse/BP differential assessed and red flags recognized: Crew performs a full assessment including bilateral pulses and blood pressures, identifies the asymmetry and tearing chest-to-back pain as concerning for aortic dissection, provides cautious analgesia, and prepares for gentle transport to an appropriate specialty center. → Specialty transport initiated with gentle handling: Patient is packaged and transported gently to a facility capable of managing a suspected aortic emergency, with ongoing reassessment of pain, pulses, and vital signs throughout transport.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Sudden tearing chest pain radiating to the back

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 65-year-old male with sudden-onset severe tearing chest pain radiating to the back, pale and diaphoretic, with a markedly elevated and asymmetric blood pressure between arms.

scenarioEvents.name: Pulse/BP differential assessed and red flags recognized
scenarioEvents.description: Crew performs a full assessment including bilateral pulses and blood pressures, identifies the asymmetry and tearing chest-to-back pain as concerning for aortic dissection, provides cautious analgesia, and prepares for gentle transport to an appropriate specialty center.
relatedChecklist: Assess bilateral pulses and blood pressures for asymmetry; recognize as a red flag for aortic emergency
Obtain vascular access to allow analgesia administration
Fentanyl 85 mcg IV (85 kg x 1 mcg/kg = 85 mcg; max initial 100 mcg)
Position of comfort; minimize exertion and handle gently to avoid further BP spikes

scenarioEvents.name: Specialty transport initiated with gentle handling
scenarioEvents.description: Patient is packaged and transported gently to a facility capable of managing a suspected aortic emergency, with ongoing reassessment of pain, pulses, and vital signs throughout transport.
relatedChecklist: Transport to a specialty destination center for suspected aortic emergency; minimize scene time
Reassess vital signs and response to analgesia throughout transport

scenarioEvents.name: Deterioration into hypotension and shock
scenarioEvents.description: The patient suddenly develops hypotension and worsening tachycardia en route, consistent with rupture or cardiac tamponade from the dissection. Crew must recognize and manage evolving shock per the Shock Guideline.
relatedChecklist: Recognize shock and initiate treatment per the Shock Guideline; cautious fluids, prepare for rapid transport
